environmentalProblems.title: Environmental Problems
environmentalProblems.subtitle: Understand the main environmental challenges we face and their impact on global climate change.
environmentalProblems.cardDescription: Introductory document explaining current major environmental problems, their causes and consequences for the planet and society.
environmentalProblems.description: They are negative alterations in the natural environment mainly caused by human activities. These problems affect climate, biodiversity, health, and quality of life on the planet.
environmentalProblems.globalWarmingDesc: Increase in the planet's average temperature due to greenhouse gas emissions.
environmentalProblems.pollutionDesc: Presence of toxic substances that harm health and ecosystems.
environmentalProblems.deforestationDesc: Loss of forests due to logging and agricultural expansion, reducing biodiversity.
environmentalProblems.wasteDesc: Accumulation of garbage and plastics that pollute soils and oceans.
environmentalProblems.energyDesc: Excessive use of energy from non-renewable sources.
environmentalProblems.cause1: Burning of fossil fuels (coal, oil, gas).
environmentalProblems.consequence1: Increase in extreme weather events (hurricanes, droughts, floods).
environmentalProblems.consequence3: Public health problems (respiratory diseases, lack of drinking water).
environmentalProblems.consequence4: Displacement of communities and increased poverty.
environmentalProblems.keyFactDesc: More than 70% of greenhouse gases come from energy, industry, and agriculture.
environmentalProblems.didYouKnowDesc: Every year millions of hectares of forest are lost and more than 300 million tons of plastic are generated.

sustainabilityReports.title: Guide to Preparing Sustainability Reports
sustainabilityReports.subtitle: Learn how to communicate your organization's environmental, social, and economic performance and strengthen transparency and sustainability.
sustainabilityReports.cardDescription: Practical manual for designing sustainability strategies aligned with the SDGs, with steps, examples and recommendations.
sustainabilityReports.description: It is a document that communicates an organization's environmental, social, and economic performance. It informs stakeholders about the impact of activities and commitment to sustainable development.
sustainabilityReports.organizationalContextDesc: Description of the company, mission, vision, and values.
sustainabilityReports.materialityDesc: Relevant topics for the organization and its stakeholders.
sustainabilityReports.environmentalPerformanceDesc: Resource consumption, emissions, waste management, and environmental actions.
sustainabilityReports.socialPerformanceDesc: Working conditions, human rights, diversity, health, and safety.
sustainabilityReports.economicPerformanceDesc: Financial results, value generation, and local development.
sustainabilityReports.benefit1: Improves transparency and trust with stakeholders.
sustainabilityReports.benefit4: Contributes to compliance with international regulations and standards (GRI).
sustainabilityReports.step4Desc: Prepare and validate the document internally.
sustainabilityReports.standardsDesc: The GRI (Global Reporting Initiative) framework is the most widely used. Integrate the SDGs (Sustainable Development Goals) into strategy and reporting.

socioEnvironmentalComponents.title: Socio-environmental Components of an Organization
socioEnvironmentalComponents.subtitle: Discover how social and environmental components interact in the sustainable management of an organization.
socioEnvironmentalComponents.cardDescription: Conceptual framework on the social and environmental elements that integrate the sustainable management of an organization.
socioEnvironmentalComponents.description: They are the social and environmental elements that make up the structure and functioning of an organization, and that influence its sustainability and responsibility.
socioEnvironmentalComponents.socialComponentDesc: People, organizational culture, labor relations, well-being, equity, diversity, and inclusion. It involves promoting a healthy work environment, participation, and social responsibility.
socioEnvironmentalComponents.environmentalComponentDesc: Natural resources used (water, energy, materials), emissions, waste, and the impact of activities on the environment. It seeks to minimize negative impact, promote efficiency, and regulatory compliance.
socioEnvironmentalComponents.importance1: Integrating both components allows the organization to be sustainable, improve its reputation, and comply with regulations.
socioEnvironmentalComponents.importance2: Sustainability requires balance between economic development, social well-being, and environmental protection.
socioEnvironmentalComponents.action1: Diagnosis of social and environmental aspects.
socioEnvironmentalComponents.action2: Implementation of social and environmental responsibility policies.
socioEnvironmentalComponents.action4: Measurement and reporting of performance indicators.
socioEnvironmentalComponents.keyFactDesc: Effective socio-environmental management drives sustainability, innovation, and organizational competitiveness.

threatsImpactsAspects.title: Threats, Impacts, and Environmental Aspects
threatsImpactsAspects.subtitle: Learn to identify, evaluate, and manage environmental risks and consequences in your organization to drive sustainability.
threatsImpactsAspects.cardDescription: Guide to identify and evaluate threats, impacts and environmental aspects in the organizational context.
threatsImpactsAspects.whatAre: What are threats, impacts, and environmental aspects?
threatsImpactsAspects.threatsDesc: Factors or activities that can cause harm to the environment, such as pollution, deforestation, excessive use of natural resources, and climate change.
threatsImpactsAspects.impactsDesc: Direct or indirect consequences of threats, such as loss of biodiversity, soil degradation, water and air pollution, and global warming.
threatsImpactsAspects.aspectsDesc: Elements of an organization's activities, products, or services that can interact with the environment, for example, energy consumption, waste generation, atmospheric emissions, and water use.
threatsImpactsAspects.management1: Identify and evaluate significant environmental aspects.
threatsImpactsAspects.management2: Implement controls and best practices to minimize negative impacts.
threatsImpactsAspects.management3: Adopt sustainability policies and clean technologies.
threatsImpactsAspects.benefit4: Contribution to planet protection and social well-being.
threatsImpactsAspects.keyFactDesc: Proactive management of threats and environmental aspects is fundamental to achieving sustainability and preventing irreversible damage to the environment.

responsibleConsumption.title: Actions for Responsible Consumption
responsibleConsumption.subtitle: Responsible consumption involves making informed and conscious decisions about the products and services we acquire, considering their environmental, social, and economic impact. Adopting responsible consumption habits is fundamental to reducing carbon footprint and promoting sustainability.
responsibleConsumption.cardDescription: Strategies and recommendations for implementing responsible consumption practices.
responsibleConsumption.action1Desc: Before buying, ask yourself if you really need it.
responsibleConsumption.action2Desc: Prefer products with low environmental impact, locally sourced, and with ecological certifications.
responsibleConsumption.action3Desc: Give objects a second life and properly separate waste for recycling.
responsibleConsumption.action4Desc: Turn off lights and devices when not in use, and use water efficiently.
responsibleConsumption.action5Desc: Walk, use a bicycle, or public transport to reduce emissions.
responsibleConsumption.action6Desc: Favor local agriculture and reduce transportation footprint.
responsibleConsumption.action7Desc: Prefer reusable containers and reduce plastic use.
responsibleConsumption.benefit3: Promotion of local and fair economies.
responsibleConsumption.benefit4: Reduction of personal and collective carbon footprint.
responsibleConsumption.keyFactDesc: Every small action counts. Responsible consumption is a powerful tool to care for the planet and build a more just and sustainable society.

waterUse.title: Efficient Use and Water Conservation
waterUse.subtitle: Water is a vital and limited resource. Its efficient use and conservation are fundamental for environmental sustainability, cost reduction, and ecosystem protection. Adopting best practices ensures its availability for present and future generations.
waterUse.cardDescription: Practical guide to optimize water use and reduce waste.
waterUse.keyPrinciples: Key principles for efficient water use:
waterUse.principle1Desc: Regularly check facilities and equipment to avoid losses.
waterUse.principle2Desc: Use technologies and methods that reduce water consumption in daily and productive activities.
waterUse.principle3Desc: Implement collection and reuse systems for gray or rainwater.
waterUse.principle4Desc: Promote internal and external campaigns on the importance of water conservation.
waterUse.principle5: Responsible use at home and business:
waterUse.principle5Desc: Turn off taps when not in use, use efficient appliances, and water during appropriate hours.
waterUse.benefits: Benefits of efficient water use and conservation:
waterUse.benefit1: Reduction of operational costs and bills.
waterUse.benefit2: Decreased environmental impact and preservation of water sources.
waterUse.benefit3: Improved image and social responsibility of the organization.
waterUse.benefit4: Contribution to water security and climate change adaptation.
waterUse.action1: Install water-saving devices (aerators, low-flow toilets, sensors).
waterUse.action2: Train staff and community on responsible habits.
waterUse.action3: Monitor and record consumption to identify improvement opportunities.
waterUse.action4: Encourage innovation in water use and treatment.
waterUse.keyFactDesc: Only 2.5% of the planet's water is fresh and less than 1% is available for human consumption. Every drop counts.

energyUse.title: Efficient Energy Use and Conservation
energyUse.subtitle: Efficient energy use is key to reducing costs, decreasing greenhouse gas emissions, and contributing to environmental sustainability. Energy is an essential resource, and its optimization benefits both organizations and the planet.
energyUse.cardDescription: Recommendations and strategies to optimize energy consumption and reduce environmental impact.
energyUse.keyPrinciples: Key principles for efficient energy use:
energyUse.principle1Desc: Identify improvement opportunities through periodic technical evaluations.
energyUse.principle2Desc: Use low-consumption technology and automation to reduce waste.
energyUse.principle3Desc: Integrate clean sources such as solar, wind, or biomass.
energyUse.principle4Desc: Educate staff and community about energy conservation.
energyUse.principle5Desc: Ensure optimal equipment operation to avoid unnecessary consumption.
energyUse.principle6Desc: Implement monitoring and control systems to optimize energy use.
energyUse.principle7Desc: Consider energy efficiency criteria in infrastructure and processes from conception.
energyUse.benefit1: Reduction of operational costs and increased competitiveness.
energyUse.benefit2: Decrease in CO₂ emissions and other pollutants.
energyUse.benefit3: Regulatory compliance and improvement in environmental management.
energyUse.benefit4: Strengthening of corporate image and social responsibility.
energyUse.action1: Replace traditional lighting with LED and take advantage of natural light.
energyUse.action2: Turn off equipment and disconnect devices when not in use.
energyUse.action3: Adjust climate control systems and thermally insulate spaces.
energyUse.action4: Encourage sustainable transportation and remote work when possible.
energyUse.keyFactDesc: Energy efficiency can reduce consumption by up to 30% without affecting productivity, and is one of the most effective ways to combat climate change.

carbonFootprint.title: What is Carbon Footprint?
carbonFootprint.subtitle: Learn the fundamentals of greenhouse gas measurement and its impact on climate change.
carbonFootprint.description: Carbon footprint is a measure of the total greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions caused directly or indirectly by an activity, organization, event, or product, expressed as carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2eq).
carbonFootprint.globalImportanceDesc: Calculating carbon footprint is fundamental to understanding our impact on climate change and taking measures to reduce it.
carbonFootprint.businessBenefitsDesc: Companies that measure and reduce their carbon footprint improve their reputation, reduce operating costs, and prepare for future regulations.
carbonFootprint.importantFactDesc: Colombia committed to reducing its GHG emissions by 51% by 2030 according to the Paris Agreement.

emissionFactors.subtitle: Official values and methodologies to convert activity data into GHG emissions.
emissionFactors.noteDesc: Emission factors are updated periodically. Always consult the most recent official sources.
emissionFactors.basedOnStandards: Based on international standards and national data.

calculatorCard.title: Start your calculation!
calculatorCard.description: Our calculator will guide you step by step to obtain a complete analysis of your organization's emissions across the three scopes defined by the GHG Protocol.
calculatorCard.instruction1: Enter the data in the established order.
calculatorCard.instruction2: Do not include units in numerical values.
calculatorCard.instruction3: Use dropdown lists where "(Choose Option)" appears.
calculatorCard.instruction4: One form for each process to calculate.
calculatorCard.instruction5: The information must correspond to the reporting period.

instructiveModal.title: INSTRUCTIONS - Greenhouse Gas Emissions Tool
instructiveModal.instruction1: Complete the greenhouse gas emissions calculation tool by entering each data point in the established order.
instructiveModal.instruction2: For cells that require numerical values, do not include units, these are provided by the tool. Example: kg, gallons, m3, degrees (°), minutes (´), etc.
instructiveModal.instruction3: When "(Choose Option)" appears in the form, drop down the list to fill in the cell.
instructiveModal.instruction4: If you want to perform the calculation for more than one process, you must fill out one form for each one.
instructiveModal.instruction5: Remember that the information you fill in must correspond to the quantities for the reporting period.
instructiveModal.instruction6: Verify before entering company information that the tool does not have any data already filled in.
instructiveModal.instruction7: Avoid manipulating the "Summary" tab. Do not enter or delete information. This spreadsheet ensures the proper functioning of the tool.
instructiveModal.instruction8: Do not delete already created report sheets. To not affect the tool's operation, do not delete reports, leave them unfilled.
instructiveModal.carbonDepositsDesc: Compartments where carbon from continental ecosystems and their products is stored. Ex: above and below ground biomass, dead organic matter, soil carbon, harvested wood products.
instructiveModal.co2Desc: Gas produced naturally and as a by-product of fossil fuel and biomass combustion, land use changes, and industrial processes. Main anthropogenic GHG.
instructiveModal.co2eDesc: Unit that compares the global warming potential of each GHG relative to CO2.
instructiveModal.ghgEmissionDesc: Release of the mass of a GHG into the atmosphere.
instructiveModal.directEmissionsDesc: From sources owned or controlled by the reporting company.
instructiveModal.fugitiveEmissionsDesc: Not physically controlled but result from intentional or unintentional releases of GHG (joints, seals, gaskets, etc.).
instructiveModal.indirectEmissionsDesc: Consequence of operations by the reporting company, but occur at sources owned/controlled by other companies.
instructiveModal.referenceScenarioDesc: Baseline representing GHG emissions that would occur in the absence of mitigation policies or initiatives.
instructiveModal.emissionFactorDesc: Allows estimating GHG emissions from activity data and total GHG emissions.
instructiveModal.ghgDesc: Gaseous components of the atmosphere that absorb and re-emit infrared radiation.
instructiveModal.gwpDesc: Factor describing the impact of a unit mass of a GHG relative to CO2 over a specific period.

questions.A_q_2: The company continuously identifies innovations to improve its products and processes.

questions.A_q_5: The quality of the product/service is consistent and meets client expectations.
questions.A_q_6: The company receives a price that generates a reasonable and sustainable profit margin.
questions.A_q_7: Sales are distributed among several clients (there is no dependence on one or a few specific clients).
questions.A_q_8: Sales per client increase each year.
questions.A_q_9: The products/services offered by the company reflect competitive advantages over substitutes.
questions.A_q_10: The company knows the weaknesses of its main competitors and has developed strategies to take advantage of them.
questions.A_q_11: The company directly manages the distribution and commercialization channels of its products.
questions.A_q_12: The company generates competitive advantages by providing additional services to the product.

questions.A_q_15: In recent years the company has managed to enter new markets.
questions.A_q_16: The company keeps its sales records updated.
questions.A_q_17: The company's collection mechanisms are effective.
questions.A_q_18: The company has internal controls that allow it to detect deviations between the projected and executed in an early manner.

questions.A_q_24: The company and/or organization includes environmental aspects in financial processes through technical-economic-financial methods.

questions.B_q_30: Before making large investments (For example, in new facilities, machinery or equipment) the impact of these on the environment is investigated.
questions.B_q_31: The company has managed to ensure broad support for environmental management through established discussion groups and structures.

questions.B_q_33: Wherever possible, the company uses clean energy (generated through wind energy, solar energy, gas and/or cogeneration).
